text: Ah, the man with the cat. Come, sit. I have things you cannot afford and a few you can.
heard: Ah, the man with the cat. Come, sit. I have things you cannot afford, and a few you can.

text: Look who crawled in from Giza. Sit down before you fall down.
heard: Look who crawled in from Giza, sit down before you fall down.

text: Welcome, welcome, pasha of the three rugs. Tea first. Then I rob you.
heard: Welcome, welcome, Pasha of the three rugs. T first. Then I rob you.

text: You again? Good. A merchant who comes back is a merchant who is selling. Or begging.
heard: You again, good. A merchant who comes back is a merchant who is selling or begging.

text: Come in, nephew. Mind the doorstep. It is worth more than your stall.
heard: Come in, nephew. Mind the doorstep. It is worth more than your stall.

text: Ahlan! I heard you coming from Bab Zuweila. Nobody else walks like a lost goat.
heard: Ah, lahn, I heard you coming from Babzuayla. Nobody else walks like a lost goat.

text: Sit. Drink. Say nothing clever. My heart is old.
heard: Sit, drink, say nothing clever, my heart is old.

text: The tram stopped outside and I prayed it was a rich Englishman. It was you. God is testing me.
heard: The tram stopped outside and I prayed it was a rich Englishman. It was you. God is testing me.

text: You drive a hard bargain for a man with three rugs. Fine. Take it and go before I wake up.
heard: You drive a hard bargain for a man with three rugs. Fine. Take it and go before I wake up.

text: Fine! For your father. He will laugh at me over backgammon tonight, I know it.
heard: Fine for your father. He will laugh at me over Bagamun tonight. I know it.

text: You haggle like a Khan el-Khalili grandmother. I am proud and I am ruined.
heard: You haggle like a Chanel-Hallee grandmother. I am proud and I am ruined.

text: Take it. My children will eat bread and onions tonight, and it is your fault.
heard: Take it. My children will eat bread and onions tonight. And it is your fault.

text: Where did you learn that? Not from me. I would never teach you to rob me.
heard: Where did you learn that? Not from me. I would never teach you to rob me.

text: Fine, fine. Write it down, the day Rashid lost. Nobody will believe you.
heard: Fine, fine, write it down. The day Rashid lost. Nobody will believe you.

text: You win. Now stop smiling, it does not suit you.
heard: You win. Now stop smiling. He does not suit you.

text: Mabrouk. You have bought something that will not embarrass you. For once.
heard: Babruk, you have bought something that will not embarrass you. For once.

text: Go on, show it to the Englishwomen. They will pay anything if you say it is old.
heard: Go on, show it to the English women. They will pay anything if you say it is old.

text: I will write it in the book. Five days. Do not make me come to Giza. I hate Giza.
heard: I will write it in the book. Five days. Do not make me come to Giza. I hate Giza.

text: Credit, he says. Fine. My book is heavier than the Pharaoh's coffin, one more line will not hurt.
heard: "Ready," he says. "Fine. My book is heavier than the pharaoh's coffin. One more line will not hurt."

text: I write your name in the book next to the pasha who ran off to Paris. Do not join him.
heard: I write your name in the book next to the Pasha who ran off to Paris. Do not join him.

text: On credit. God help me, I am soft like fresh bread.
heard: On credit, God help me. I am soft like fresh bread.

text: Take it. Pay me on time and I will stop shouting. A little.
heard: Hmm, take it. Pay me on time and I will stop shouting. A little...

text: Written down. The ink is permanent, nephew, and so is my memory.
heard: Written down. The ink is permanent nephew, and so is my memory.

text: Credit? You have not earned credit yet. You have barely earned a chair.
heard: Credit? You have not earned credit yet. You have barely earned a chair.

text: No credit. Even the Bank Misr would laugh you out the door.
heard: No credit. Even the bank-misser would laugh you out the door.

text: Credit for you? My book says no, my heart says no, and my wife says absolutely not.
heard: credit for you? My book says no, my heart says no, and my wife says absolutely not.

text: Pay me what you owe first. Then we talk about owing me more.
heard: Pay me what you owe first. Then we talk about owing me more.

text: The book is closed to you today. Sell something, then come back smiling.
heard: The book is closed to you today. Sell something, then come back smiling.

text: Credit is for men who pay. You are a man who promises.
heard: Credit is for men who pay. You are a man who promises.

text: Your stall is so small the flies queue outside.
heard: Your stall is so small, the fly is Q outside.

text: Did you hear? Another Englishman fainted in Tutankhamun's tomb. I think he saw the price of your rugs.
heard: Did you hear? Another Englishman fainted in Tutankhamun's tomb. I think he saw the price of your rugs.

text: You know the pasha across the street? He owes me more than you. It makes me love you a little.
heard: You know the Pasha across the street. He owes me more than you. It makes me love you a little.

text: The trams go faster every year. And still you arrive late.
heard: The trams go faster every year, and still you arrive late.

text: They say cotton is down again. Good. Now the cotton men haggle like you. Badly.
heard: They say cotton is down again. Good. Now the cotton men hug like you. Badly.

text: Everybody in the Khan asks me about you. I tell them you are my nephew. Then I apologise.
heard: Everybody in the Han asks me about you. I tell them you are my nephew. Then I apologize.

text: The Wafd wants independence. I want my money. We are both still waiting.
heard: The waft wants independence. I want my money. We are both still waiting.

text: My tea boy sells more than you, and he only sells tea.
heard: My tea boy sells more than you and he only sells tea.

text: You call that a stall? I have seen bigger stalls on a donkey cart.
heard: You call that stall? I have seen bigger stalls on a donkey cart.

text: Lord Carnarvon died of a curse. You will die of haggling. It is slower.
heard: Lord Carnarvon died of a curse. You will die of haggling. It is slower.

text: Tell me honestly, do you sell rugs, or do you just sit on them?
heard: Tell me honestly, do sell drugs or do you just sit on them?

text: An Englishwoman asked me today if the pyramids were for sale. I sent her to you. You owe me.
heard: An English woman asked me today if the pyramids were for sale. I sent her to you. You owe me.

text: I have known you since you were this tall. You were cleverer then.
heard: I have known you since you are this tall. You are cleverer then.
